thread:
lucy_cs: FYI escalating a live customer report — AcmeMedia on Dedicated (EU) says Hindi->English translations are now getting random Cantonese fragments after today's model rollout. They included a repro and a request_id. @hiro_prod can you triage?

customer_acme: Quote from their support email: "We used to get clean English summaries. After the deploy at ~10:30 UTC, several responses suddenly include zh snippets (e.g. \u2018香港\u2019) in the middle of English text. This breaks our downstream parsers. Sample prompt + output below. Request ID: req_eu_0b9c1f"

customer_acme: ```
prompt: "Summarize the following Hindi article in English: <article>..."
output: "Summary: This article discusses... 香港... it also notes..."
```

lucy_cs: They say it started immediately after the canary shift. No 5xxs on their side. No auth/billing errors.

hiro_prod: Can you paste the full request payload (headers) + request_id? Also which model/route they hit (route name or model name). I'll grep router logs for req_eu_0b9c1f.

lucy_cs: Request ID: req_eu_0b9c1f. Payload (redacted):
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
X-Route: redwood-eu-text-v2
Model: redwood-open-mid-7b
body: {"prompt": "Summarize in English...", "temperature": 0.0}
```

miguel_eng: Quick thought: sounds like a routing/matcher bug where locale tag "hi" accidentally matched a zh-optimized model variant during the canary. We shipped a small routing regex change in the canary config this morning. Can someone check router config for locale rules?

priya_support: Customer confirms temperature=0.0 and deterministic sampling. They provided a longer failing example and a link to logs: https://files.redwood.com/acme/req_eu_0b9c1f.log (internal)

deploy-bot: Canary rollout redwood/text-serving-config @ 2026-11-05T10:25:41Z: traffic 50% -> variant A (includes locale-matcher update). CI: green.

hiro_prod: Found it — the regex we added to match language tags had an accidental character class: `/(zh|cn|zh-CN|hi)/i` instead of `/(zh|cn|zh-CN)/i`. That means "hi" matched the zh branch when the router evaluated locale heuristics. Grepping logs: router.match(req_eu_0b9c1f) -> variant_zh.

miguel_eng: Oof. Patch suggested: change matcher to explicit lists per locale and add unit for "hi" -> hi-model. I'll push a hotfix to roll back the canary change and update the rule.

miguel_eng: Pushed rollback, restarted router process on two EU router pods. Commands: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/router-eu` and `curl -sS http://router-eu/health` returned OK.

lucy_cs: Sent hotfix note to customer and asked them to re-run the same prompt.

customer_acme: Re-tested. "Looks good now — English summaries restored, no Cantonese snippets. Thanks! :thumbsup:"

priya_support: Leaving this open until we have a short postmortem + runbook update (prevent locale regex regressions).

lucy_cs: Agreed — I'll create a quick incident note and add matcher unit tests + an ops checklist for canaries. Moving to follow-up. :memo:
